title: Removing pure-point harmonic spectrum and imposing W3,1 density gives integrable electric and holonomy amplitudes

spectral_exclusion.decomposition: Decompose E_h into a finite pure-point trigonometric polynomial plus an absolutely continuous Fourier integral with densities F_+ and F_-.
spectral_exclusion.atomic_obstruction: Every nonzero finite pure-point trigonometric polynomial has positive mean absolute value and infinite time L1 norm; K1589 and K1599 are one-frequency instances.
spectral_exclusion.exact_exclusion: Impose P_pp E_h=0, so every declared nondispersive atomic resonant sector is excluded rather than only the homogeneous matter mode.
spectral_exclusion.density_hypothesis: Assume F_+,F_- are W^{3,1}, supported away from zero, with their values and first two derivatives zero at every support endpoint.
spectral_exclusion.decay: Three integrations by parts give |E_h(t)|<=t^(-3)B_3 for t>=1, where B_3=||F_+'''||_1+||F_-'''||_1.
spectral_exclusion.budgets: With B_0=||F_+||_1+||F_-||_1, int|E_h|<=B_0+B_3/2. If a(infinity)=0 and a(t)=int_t^infinity E_h(s)ds, then int|a|<=B_0/2+B_3 and ||a||_infinity<=B_0+B_3/2.
spectral_exclusion.scope_guard: The spectral and endpoint hypotheses are sufficient, not necessary, and are not derived here from the nonlinear Maxwell-matter equations or a source-owned action.
